target: An orifice ring (the raised ring at the throat of the calyx tube in Asarum) is absent, on the calyx tube (FLOPO_0986011). The calyx (PO:0009060) is present. Neither PO nor FLOPO has a class for the orifice ring, so make no absence annotation for now
fix: In '<sub-structure> absent', the noun before 'absent' is the absent part, and the organ under description is only where it would be. 'orifice ring absent', 'throat ring absent' and 'annulus absent' deny a ring on the calyx/perianth tube, never the calyx. If the sub-structure has no class, drop the statement rather than falling back to the organ.
reason: The calyx is described as adaxially pubescent, so it exists. Only the ring at its mouth is missing.

target: No absence. The whole plant (PO:0000003) is holomycotrophic (FLOPO:0991374), which the other statement already records. 'Without chlorophyll' is that trophic quality, not a missing part
fix: 'without chlorophyll', 'lacking chlorophyll' and 'achlorophyllous' describe how a plant feeds. Map them to holomycotrophic FLOPO:0991374 (or saprophytic FLOPO:0991360 when the flora says so) on the whole plant, never to 'whole plant absent'. Chlorophyll is a substance, not a part, so it can never take a part absence.
reason: A plant that is described cannot be absent. The phrase names a missing pigment.

target: Only the basal sheaths have no blade: leaf lamina (PO:0020039) absent with context basal (FLOPO_0991002), on leaf sheath (PO:0020104). Otherwise the culm is aphyllopodic (FLOPO:0991233). The blades of the other leaves are present, with scabrous margins
fix: In sedges and grasses, 'bladeless sheaths' and 'basal sheaths bladeless' describe only the lowest, sheath-only leaves. Never record a taxon-wide 'leaf lamina absent'. Keep 'basal' as the context, or map the culm to aphyllopodic FLOPO:0991233.
reason: Carex leaves have blades. Only the basal sheaths lack them, and the blade margins are described as scabrous.

target: Leaf lamina (PO:0020039) absent only on the basal sheaths, context basal (FLOPO_0991002). The sheaths are yellow-brown and lustrous. The blades of the other leaves are present and papillose
fix: Same as 'bladeless sheaths': colour or lustre words in front of 'bladeless sheaths' still describe the basal sheaths. The absence stays limited to those basal members.
reason: Same Carex pattern. The papillose blades exist.

target: No bract absence. In Carex, 'without distinct involucral bract leaf' means the bract (PO:0009055) has no leaf-like blade: it is short and glume-like. The red-brown involucral bracts are present
fix: 'without (a) distinct <X> leaf' and 'bract not leaflike' deny the leaf-like form or blade of the bract, never the bract. Record it as the bract's lamina being absent or reduced, or drop it. Never record 'bract absent'. 'Distinct' signals that the part is reduced, not missing.
reason: The same taxon has red-brown involucral bracts, so the bracts are there. Only a leafy one is lacking.

target: Leaf lamina (PO:0020039) absent only on the basal sheaths, context basal (FLOPO_0991002). The blades of the other leaves are flat
fix: Same as 'bladeless sheaths': quantity or colour words ('few brownish and bladeless sheaths') still refer to the basal sheaths. Keep 'basal' as the context and never record a taxon-wide 'leaf lamina absent'.
reason: The flat blades exist. Only the basal sheaths lack blades.

target: The bracts (PO:0009055) have no sheath: a sheath (leaf sheath PO:0020104, as part of the bract) is absent. The bracts themselves are present. The glume statement is unrelated and correct
fix: In Carex bract descriptions, 'without sheaths', 'sheathless' and 'not sheathing' deny the sheath at the bract base, never the bract. The absent part is 'sheath'. The organ under description is only where it would be.
reason: The subject of 'without sheaths' is the bracts, which are present. The checker linked it to the glume because a glume is a kind of bract.

target: A basal lobe is absent on one margin of the fruit bract (PO:0009055), usually the inner margin, while the outer margin has an ovate, inflexed basal lobe. The bract is present. 'Ovate' belongs to the lobe, not to the whole bract
fix: In Carpinus, 'without basal lobe' and 'with ... basal lobe' describe the two margins of the same bract (inner and outer). Map them to a lobe of the bract with an inner or outer context, never to the bract. A shape inside 'with <shape> basal lobe' belongs to the lobe.
reason: Carpinus fruit bracts are typically described margin by margin. One margin has a lobe and the other does not.

target: Leaf (PO:0025034) absent with context basal (FLOPO_0991002). Only the basal leaves are missing. The stem leaves (the bract-like leaves) are present and petiolate
fix: 'basal leaves absent' and 'without basal leaves' must keep the qualifier 'basal' (FLOPO_0991002) as the context of the absence. A qualified absence never becomes 'leaf absent'.
reason: The leaves on the flowering stems are described with petioles. Only the basal ones are lacking.

target: The stem or scape is leafless: cauline leaf (PO:0000013) absent. The basal leaves are present, with entire, revolute margins
fix: A bare 'leafless' in a stem or scape sentence ('stem/scape leafless') means no cauline leaves (PO:0000013) on that axis. In rosette or scapose herbs, never read it as 'leaf absent' for the whole taxon.
reason: The leaves of the same Crepis are described with revolute margins, so they are basal leaves, and 'leafless' refers to the stem.

target: No absence. The stem is almost leafless: cauline leaves (PO:0000013) are few or much reduced. The basal leaves are present and narrowly lanceolate
fix: Words that hedge ('almost leafless', '± leafless', 'nearly leafless', 'subscapose') mean few or reduced stem leaves, never absent ones. Drop the absence, or record a reduced number of cauline leaves on the stem.
reason: 'Almost' rules out absence, and the lanceolate leaves exist.

target: Leaf sheath auricle (PO:0020106) absent, on the culm sheath (leaf sheath PO:0020104). The other statement is also misread: 'Culm sheaths deciduous' is leaf sheath (PO:0020104) deciduous (PATO:0001730), not 'stipule present'
fix: In bamboos, 'auricles' always means sheath auricles (PO:0020106) and 'culm sheath' means a leaf sheath (PO:0020104) of the culm. Neither is a stipule. Remove any 'auricle → stipule' or 'sheath → stipule' mapping in Poaceae.
reason: Bamboos have no stipules. Both statements were sent to 'stipule' by a wrong mapping.

target: The stem is leafless in its lower part (region: proximal): cauline leaf (PO:0000013) absent there. The leaves higher up are present, with dentate margins
fix: 'leafless in lower part', 'leafless below' and 'leafless at base' limit the absence to a stem region. Keep the region (lower part → proximal) and never record a taxon-wide 'leaf absent'.
reason: The leaves are described with mucronulate-dentate margins, so leaves exist higher up.

target: Lower glume (PO:0006002) absent (PATO:0000462). The upper glume is present and appressed-pubescent
fix: 'lower glume absent' must map to lower glume PO:0006002, never to glume PO:0009039. In grasses, 'lower glume' and 'first glume' are fixed terms for that member, not a free 'lower' context on 'glume'.
reason: In Digitaria the lower glume is often absent or minute, while the upper glume is described. The member was lost when it was mapped to the general class.

target: No absence: the flowers are unknown (not collected). The pubescent inflorescence or infructescence statement stands
fix: 'not seen', 'not known', 'unknown' and 'not observed' mean the flora's authors lacked material. They never mean absent. Drop such statements. At most, record that the data is missing, never PATO:0000462.
reason: Diospyros has flowers. The flora only says the specimens lacked them.

target: The ray achenes (achenes of the ray florets) have no pappus, while the disc achenes have a bristly pappus (PO:0025393). Context: ray floret vs disc floret
fix: In Asteraceae, 'without pappus' next to a described pappus usually belongs to one kind of floret or achene ('ray achenes without pappus'). Take the floret kind (ray/disc, marginal/central) from the sentence subject as the context of the absence. If no context is found, do not record a taxon-wide 'pappus absent'.
reason: Doronicum often has ray achenes without a pappus and disc achenes with bristles. Both statements hold for different florets.

target: Leaf sheath auricle (PO:0020106) absent, and oral setae (trichome PO:0000282 at the sheath shoulder) absent, on the culm or leaf sheath (PO:0020104). The 'glabrous' statement belongs to the sheath, not to a stipule
fix: In bamboos, 'auricles and oral setae absent' is an absence of sheath auricles (PO:0020106) and of the shoulder bristles (trichome PO:0000282), with the sheath as location. Never map it to stipule or leaf.
reason: Bamboos have no stipules. Both statements reached 'stipule' through a wrong auricle mapping.

target: The capitulum has no calyculus: the outer supplementary bracts (bract PO:0009055) at the base of the involucre are absent, context outer (FLOPO_0991379). The phyllaries (involucral bract PO:0009045) are present and glabrous
fix: In Asteraceae, 'not bracteate', 'ecalyculate' and 'without calyculus' in an involucre or capitulum sentence deny only the outer calyculus bracts. Never record 'bract absent' or 'involucral bract absent' when phyllaries are described.
reason: Emilia has a single row of phyllaries and no calyculus. The phyllaries themselves are described as glabrous.

target: No absence. Stipule (PO:0020041) deciduous (PATO:0001730) only. 'Not seen' means the stipules had already fallen from the specimens
fix: 'caducous, not seen' and 'early caducous, not observed' mean the part falls early. Map them to deciduous (PATO:0001730) and never also emit an absence.
reason: The same phrase says the stipules are caducous, so they exist for a short time.

target: Leaf sheath auricle (PO:0020106) absent. The other statement is misread too: 'ligule brown' is ligule (PO:0020105) brown, not leaf brown
fix: In grasses and bamboos, 'auricles absent' maps to leaf sheath auricle PO:0020106 and 'ligule …' to ligule PO:0020105. Never generalise either to 'leaf'. When the named sub-part has a PO class, the annotation must use it.
reason: The leaf is clearly present. Both statements lost their actual part.

target: Leaf sheath auricle (PO:0020106) absent (PATO:0000462), and oral setae (trichome PO:0000282) absent. The second record wrongly turns the same absence sentence into an auricle presence
fix: In 'A and B absent', 'absent' applies to every member of the list. No presence annotation may come from a phrase that ends in 'absent', 'lacking' or 'wanting'. A part named in a negated list gives an absence only.
reason: Both records quote absence text. One of them was annotated as present, so the contradiction is made by the extraction, not by the plant.

target: Leaf sheath auricle (PO:0020106) absent, and oral setae (trichome PO:0000282) absent. 'auricles and oral setae absent' was wrongly annotated as an auricle presence
fix: Same as for 'A and B absent': the negation covers the whole list, and no member of a negated list may get a presence annotation.
reason: Both texts state absence. The presence record is an extraction error.

target: Pistillode (PO:0009078) absent in male flowers (flower, context male PATO:0000384). The ovary of the female flowers (PO:0009072) is present and smooth
fix: 'rudimentary ovary absent', 'pistillode absent' and 'without rudimentary pistil' map to pistillode PO:0009078, never to plant ovary PO:0009072. They come from male-flower sentences, so keep 'male' as the context.
reason: A rudimentary ovary is the sterile pistil of a male flower. The fertile ovary of the female flowers is described.

target: Involucral bract (PO:0009045) absent (or a bract subtending the inflorescence). The glumes, which are spikelet bracts, are present, with obtuse apices
fix: 'involucral bracts absent' must map to involucral bract PO:0009045, never to the general bract PO:0009055. Otherwise every glume, lemma or bracteole of the taxon contradicts it. The modifier 'involucral' is part of the term.
reason: Glumes are bracts. A general 'bract absent' clashes with the described glumes, although only the involucral bracts are lacking.

target: Flower (PO:0009046) absent with context sterile (PATO:0000956). Only the showy sterile marginal flowers are missing. The fertile flowers and the inflorescence are present
fix: 'sterile flowers absent' and 'without sterile flowers' must keep 'sterile' (PATO:0000956) as the context of the absence, as for 'male' and 'female'. A qualified flower absence never becomes 'flower absent'.
reason: In Hydrangea, whether marginal sterile flowers are present is a standard character. The fertile flowers exist.

target: No absence: the flowers are unknown. The 'solitary' statement probably describes the fruiting inflorescence and stands
fix: 'flowers not known', 'unknown' and 'not seen' mean the material was lacking. Drop them and never map them to PATO:0000462.
reason: Ilex has flowers. The flora only lacked flowering specimens.

target: No absence: the male flowers are unknown. Male context (PATO:0000384) at most, with no quality. The female or fruiting inflorescences are axillary
fix: 'male flowers not known' and 'female flowers unknown' mean missing material for one sex. Drop them. Never record 'flower absent', and never drop the sex word.
reason: The flowers of a dioecious Ilex are only unknown for one sex.

target: The auricle (the dorsal basal lobe) of the lateral united petals is absent. The petals (PO:0009032) are present, and the upper petal is suborbicular. There is no PO class for the petal auricle, so make no absence annotation for now
fix: In Impatiens, 'auricle absent' and 'without auricle' in a lateral-petal sentence deny the dorsal auricle of the lateral united petals, never the petal. If the sub-part has no class, drop the statement rather than falling back to the petal.
reason: The petals are described, so they exist. Only their basal auricle is missing.

target: No absence. The stem or scape is '± leafless': cauline leaves (PO:0000013) are few or reduced. The pilose leaves (basal leaves) are present
fix: '±', 'almost', 'nearly' or 'sub-' in front of 'leafless' means reduced, not absent. Drop the absence. A bare 'leafless' in a stem sentence means cauline leaves absent, never 'leaf absent'.
reason: The leaves are described as pilose, and '±' rules out a firm absence.

target: Stalk (PO:0025066, stipe) absent at the base of the frond. The frond (the leaf-like body of duckweed, here mapped to leaf) is present and flat
fix: 'without <X> stalk at base' and 'without stipe' deny a stalk at the base of the organ, never the organ. Map them to stalk PO:0025066, with the organ (in Lemnoideae, the frond) as location.
reason: The frond is described as flat, so it exists. Only the green stalk is lacking.
